Bianca Nogrady
Nature, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03343-1 Some countries are introducing sweeping social-media bans for young people, but the impact of screen time is still under investigation.

item.title: Differentiable Virtual-Slot Partitioning for Adaptive Tokenization in Vision Transformers
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Gaoxiang He, Bin Zhu, Bo Xie, Xiaotong Yu, Yi Chen, Hongfei Yan
arXiv:2611.11058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive tokenization aims to reduce the compute spent on uninformative image regions while preserving accuracy. Existing work relies on (i) fixed or frozen scoring rules, which cannot be trained toward the task loss, or (ii) discrete masks trained with straight-through estimators, which yield noisy gradients, while fully differentiable alternatives instead leave the pre-trained regular grid. We revisit adaptive tokenization from a regular-grid perspective and ask: can a two-scale quadtree be learned end-to-end without deleting a single token during training? We show that one coarse token and its four fine children can be made the two endpoints of a single continuous interpolation. We introduce Differentiable Virtual-Slot Partitioning (\dvsp{}), which keeps four \emph{virtual slots} per $2{\times}2$ region and blends their token features and attention mass with a single weight $\alpha$, exactly reproducing the discrete grid at $\alpha \in \{0,1\}$. On COCO detection with EVA-02-B, \dvsp{} retains $97.9\%$ of dense Box AP while removing $64.2\%$ of visual tokens, giving a $1.61\times$ end-to-end speedup, and it outperforms entropy-based APT, DART, and uniform lower-resolution dense adaptation at matched budgets; these gains depend on the conserved attention mass, whose removal costs $1.59$ Box AP. On a frozen Segmenter it also improves Cityscapes mIoU, and on frozen DeiT backbones it exceeds entropy selection at identical per-image token counts.

item.title: Kelix Technical Report
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Boyang Ding, Chenglong Chu, Dunju Zang, Han Li, Jiangxia Cao, Kun Gai, Muhao Wei, Ruiming Tang, Shiyao Wang, Siyang Mao, Xinchen Luo, Yahui Liu, Zhixin Ling, Zhuoran Yang, Ziming Li, Chengru Song, Guorui Zhou, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Hao Wang, Jiaxin Deng, Jin Ouyang, Jinghao Zhang, Lejian Ren, Qianqian Wang, Qigen Hu, Tao Wang, Xingmei Wang, Yiping Yang, Zixing Zhang, Ziqi Wang
arXiv:2602.09843v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Autoregressive large language models (LLMs) scale well by expressing diverse tasks as sequences of discrete natural-language tokens and training with next-token prediction, which unifies comprehension and generation under self-supervision. Extending this paradigm to multimodal data requires a shared, discrete representation across modalities. However, most vision-language models (VLMs) still rely on a hybrid interface: discrete text tokens paired with continuous Vision Transformer (ViT) features. Because supervision is largely text-driven, these models are often biased toward understanding and cannot fully leverage large-scale self-supervised learning on non-text data. Recent work has explored discrete visual tokenization to enable fully autoregressive multimodal modeling, showing promising progress toward unified understanding and generation. Yet existing discrete vision tokens frequently lose information due to limited code capacity, resulting in noticeably weaker understanding than continuous-feature VLMs. We present Kelix, a fully discrete autoregressive unified model that closes the understanding gap between discrete and continuous visual representations.

item.title: Good Token Hunting: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Token Selection for Visual Geometry Transformers
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Shuhong Zheng, Michael Oechsle, Erik Sandstr\"om, Marie-Julie Rakotosaona, Federico Tombari, Igor Gilitschenski
arXiv:2605.23892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Visual geometry transformers have become powerful architectures for multi-view 3D reconstruction, enabling joint prediction of multiple 3D attributes in a feed-forward manner. However, their computational cost grows quadratically with the input sequence length due to the global attention layers inside these models. This limits both their scalability and efficiency. In this work, we address this challenge with a simple yet general strategy: restricting the number of key/value tokens that each query interacts with during global attention. To achieve effective token selection, we introduce a two-stage framework. First, an inter-frame selection step operates at the frame level to identify frames that should be preserved. Second, an intra-frame selection step further discards more redundant tokens within the selected frames. Our analysis highlights the advantage of a diversity-based strategy for inter-frame selection, which ensures broad coverage of the scene. For intra-frame selection, we show that layer-aware sparsification is necessary, with the selection process guided by the entropy of the global attention pattern. Our approach offers a superior speed-accuracy trade-off compared to existing solutions. Extensive experiments show that it accelerates visual geometry transformers by over 85% for scenes with 500 images while maintaining, or even improving, baseline performance, which hints that how our token selection strategy can play a crucial role in future applications of visual geometry transformers. Our project website is available at https://zsh2000.github.io/good-token-hunting.github.io.

item.title: Leveraging Complementary Event Frame and Voxel Representations for RGB-Guided Multimodal Pre-training
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Wentao Wu, Xiao Wang, Yi Wang, Chenglong Li, Yonghong Tian, Bin Luo
arXiv:2611.12040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose CM3AE 2.0, a unified RGB Frame and Event-Voxel/-Frame pre-training framework. By jointly learning multimodal spatiotemporal representations and exploiting latent cross-modal dependencies through cross-modal generation, the framework enhances multimodal information interaction and collaborative modeling capabilities. Specifically, we first propose an Event-aware Spatiotemporal Masked Reconstruction (ESMR) strategy to learn unified multimodal spatiotemporal representations. It leverages event responses to guide masking toward dynamically salient regions. Through spatiotemporal masked reconstruction, it learns spatial structures and their temporal variations from continuous RGB-Event observations. In addition, it incorporates multimodal fusion reconstruction and cross-modal contrastive learning to facilitate the modeling of cross-modal complementary information and the learning of shared representations. Building upon this, we further propose a Hierarchical Cross-modal Generation (HCG) strategy to learn latent cross-modal dependencies through visual and language generation. At the visual level, Event-conditioned RGB generation is performed using a pre-trained diffusion model to capture visual associations between the two modalities. At the language level, video-level text description generation based on joint RGB-Event representations establishes connections between multimodal visual features and linguistic semantics, further enriching the learning of cross-modal dependencies. Extensive experiments on four diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that CM3AE 2.0 consistently improves performance, validating the effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed pre-training framework.

item.title: On the Feasibility of Image-Based Representations for Air Traffic Complexity Estimation
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Hyewook Kim, Byul Kang, Seokbin Yoon, Keumjin Lee
arXiv:2608.11810v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Air traffic controllers perceive traffic complexity through the radar display, suggesting that a computer vision model operating on the same imagery may provide a natural architecture for modeling controller-perceived complexity; however, whether radar imagery is a viable input format for deep learning vision models remains unclear. Unlike natural images, radar images are extremely sparse and self-similar, consisting primarily of a black background and a few visually identical aircraft blobs, while small changes in aircraft positions can substantially alter sector-level complexity. To test whether a vision model can capture these operationally important differences, we encode each traffic situation as a position image supplemented by five channels representing aircraft state variables, including heading, speed, and altitude, and train a Vision Transformer (ViT) to regress four intrinsic complexity components derived from pairwise geometric relations among aircraft. The model achieves $R^2 > 0.96$ for all four components on test data, and a one-aircraft removal perturbation study shows that the change in the model's estimate is proportional to how much the removed aircraft contributed to sector complexity, rather than the same for every removal. These results demonstrate that, despite its atypical visual characteristics, the proposed image-based representation is a viable input format for air traffic complexity modeling.

item.title: TRIAD: Multimodal Retrieval across Abstraction, Constraints, and State
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Xiangyang Wu, Chen Ju, Xu Chen, Likang Peng, Jinsong Lan, Haihong Tang, Yang Hu
arXiv:2611.12364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal retrieval increasingly supports agentic systems, where user requests can involve cross-level relations, combine multiple constraints, and evolve across dialogue turns. In these settings, a highly similar result may still violate the user's requirements, while retrieved content may directly inform downstream actions without human screening. We introduce TRIAD, a multimodal retrieval benchmark for evaluating how well retrieval systems satisfy these complex, evolving requests. TRIAD comprises three tracks: abstraction, testing bidirectional retrieval between visual instances and concepts at different hierarchical levels; constraints, testing the joint satisfaction of positive and negative conditions; and state, testing the integration of requirements across dialogue turns and the updating of earlier conditions when users revise their requests. The benchmark contains six subsets, each with 1,000 queries and a fixed pool of 1,000 candidates per query, evaluated using a common multi-positive mean average precision (mAP) protocol. Simpler reference tasks and hard negatives grouped by the requirements they violate help characterize specific retrieval difficulties. We evaluate 20 configurations of 17 systems and find that no system leads across all six subsets. Performance declines with hierarchical distance, and negative-only queries generally underperform positive-only queries with the same number of constraints. Across paired tasks expressing the same final intent, multi-turn retrieval yields lower mAP in 39 of 40 configuration-domain comparisons. The benefits of explicit reasoning also vary across models and tasks. These findings highlight the gap between retrieving similar content and satisfying a complete request.

item.title: MAPA: Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation for Latent Dataset Distillation in 3D Medical Classification
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Weiqi Zhang, Hiroyuki Kubo
arXiv:2611.09956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dataset distillation (DD) synthesizes a small training set from a large one, but applying it to 3D medical classification is constrained by the memory and optimization costs of synthesizing full volumetric samples. Under a storage-equivalent budget, distilling in the latent space of a frozen autoencoder reduces this cost and fits more synthetic samples (prototypes) than in voxel space. However, class-level matching, such as distribution matching, causes prototypes to concentrate in dense latent regions while underrepresenting sparser intra-class regions, a consistent imbalance that we term prototype concentration. To address this, we propose MAPA (Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation), a latent distillation method that spreads prototypes across intra-class modes while preserving class-level matching. MAPA marks these modes with fixed anchors estimated by clustering the real latents and distributes prototypes over them through a soft assignment, together with a lightweight anti-collapse regularizer and curriculum weighting that stabilize the optimization. Across five 3D medical classification tasks, MAPA improves the aggregate balanced accuracy by +4.2 points over the strongest latent baseline while using the same number of prototypes. An exploratory severity analysis on MosMedData suggests improved worst-stratum recall without loss of normal-case specificity.

item.title: GenRM-Flow: Generators are Process-aware Reward Models in Flow Matching
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Siming Fu, Ruizhe He, Zheming Fu, Zeyue Xue, Fengkai Liu, Yufei Jiao, Jie Huang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Xuan Yang, Lihui Luo
arXiv:2611.11421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aligning video generation models with human preference depends critically on the quality of the reward model that scores generated videos. Current video reward models, however, source their reward signal from a model's representational rather than generative capacity: they either repurpose vision-language models as pixel-space scorers, or train auxiliary scoring heads on top of frozen generator features. The generator's actual ability to predict velocities, denoise latents, and produce videos plays no role in scoring its own generations. We argue that this overlooks a structural property of offline preference learning. Any preference optimization objective that approximates an offline preference dataset mathematically targets a strictly defined KL-constrained optimal policy. By isolating the reward term from this analytical solution and mapping the exact generation log-likelihood to its flow-matching surrogate, the empirical reward emerges deterministically as the relative difference in continuous-time velocity-prediction errors. We formalize this equivalence into GenRM-Flow, a framework where a preference-tuned video generator inherently operates as a process-aware reward model directly in the noisy latent space. We further show theoretically that distinct fine-tuning objectives, whether contrastive like DPO and IPO or non-contrastive like RWR, are alternative optimization pathways toward the same optimal policy, each inducing a reward readout from the generator's velocity-prediction errors. Furthermore, the extracted process reward seamlessly substitutes external VLM scorers in FlowAWR. Operating purely on native latent outputs without auxiliary reward networks, this generative reward drives measurable improvements in downstream video generation.

item.title: DinoComplete: 3D Shape Completion with Distilled Semantic Priors and State Space Models
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Furkan Mert Algan, Eckehard Steinbach
arXiv:2605.26949v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: 3D shape completion from partial scans remains challenging for unseen categories and noisy real-world observations, where geometry alone is often insufficient for inferring missing structure. We present DinoComplete, a deterministic and efficient shape completion framework that augments geometric reconstruction with voxel-aligned semantic priors distilled from DINO features. First, we construct multi-view DINO feature volumes aligned with ShapeNet data and train a student network to predict dense semantic features directly from incomplete shapes. These predicted features capture global structure and part-aware semantic context while remaining aligned with the underlying geometry. We then integrate these distilled features into a completion network, where geometric and semantic voxel representations are fused through voxel state-space modeling. To enable efficient long-range reasoning without sacrificing resolution, we introduce a Multi-Scale Voxel Mamba module that refines the fused features by combining full-grid and chunk-wise sequence modeling. Experiments on unseen ShapeNet categories and ScanNet objects show that DinoComplete achieves competitive completion quality than prior deterministic and generative based completion methods while using relatively fewer parameters, requiring lower memory, and achieving faster inference. Our results demonstrate that distilling semantic priors from visual foundation models improves generalization and robustness in 3D shape completion.

item.title: Elastic Representations via Hyperbolic Geometry
item.description:
Relevance: 22% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Arjun Ramesh Kaushik, Rudrasis Chakraborty, Nalini Ratha, Venu Govindaraju
arXiv:2611.11001v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned representations (or embeddings) are the foundation of modern machine learning systems, yet they are typically trained as fixed-size embeddings, without accounting for varying downstream resource or task constraints. Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) addresses this limitation by learning nested representations, but requires costly end-to-end retraining and does not support post hoc expansion, while Contrastive Sparse Representations (CSR) reduce training overhead via lightweight adaptors but operate at a 4x larger dimensionality. Additionally, all prior works restrict their framework towards compression only. In this work, we introduce Hyperbolic Elastic Representation Learning (HERL), a framework for learning dimension-adaptive embeddings (compression and expansion) through a lightweight adaptor without retraining the base encoder. Our key idea is to exploit the exponential capacity of hyperbolic geometry by learning a non-linear mapping from the encoder space to hyperbolic space. We train a simple MLP to downsample the representations before projecting them onto a Lorentzian and learn adaptive representations that respect the Lorentzian geometry. Our approach is model-agnostic and effective in both supervised and unsupervised settings. Through extensive experiments across image and text modalities, we show that HERL preserves downstream performance across a wide range of embedding sizes, exhibits smooth interpolation between dimensions, and achieves these benefits at a fraction of the computational cost. Code: https://github.com/arjunrkaushik/herl.

item.title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: Nature
Mingyu Wu, Zhaoguo Wang, Jiabin Wang, Zhiyuan Dong, Jingkai Yang, Qingting Li, Tianyu Huang, Chi Zhang, Ping Song, Lei Zhao, Mingqiang Li, Xiaolei Zuo, Fei Wang, Chunhai Fan, Haibo Chen
Nature, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11228-6 AutoDNA is an artificial intelligence (AI)-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments, realizing the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework.

item.title: Frequency-consistent synthesis and selective transfer for medical image analysis
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Zhuhui Wang, Jianwei Zuo, Xin Peng, Kai Zhong, Xuliang Deng, Jiajia Luo
arXiv:2611.10070v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complementary imaging is not always available, and realistic synthesis does not necessarily improve downstream analysis. Here we introduce a training framework linking medical image synthesis to task learning through adaptive frequency consistency and selective feature transfer. Image-specific frequency constraints encourage consistency of structure and detail. Features are transferred only when a teacher using synthetic images achieves a lower task-error score than the student by a task-specific margin on a labelled training sample. Evaluations across five datasets show improved translation fidelity with three adversarial and diffusion-based translators trained without paired supervision, alongside gains in brain-tumour segmentation on tumour-containing slices and lesion centre-point detection. All 105 reported paired comparisons yielded point estimates favouring the proposed methods, including 36 external translation comparisons on post?treatment MRI without retraining. These findings support synthetic modalities as task-oriented complements to acquired scans when complementary imaging is unavailable.

item.title: FIELDS: Face reconstruction with accurate Inference of Expression using Learning with Direct Supervision
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Chen Ling, Henglin Shi, Hedvig Kjellstr\"om
arXiv:2511.21245v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Monocular 3D face reconstruction estimates the parameters of a 3D morphable face model (3DMM) from a single image, providing an explicit geometric representation for facial expression analysis. Owing to the scarcity of paired 2D images and 3D facial meshes, most methods are trained in a self-supervised manner by rendering the predicted face and minimizing image-level reconstruction losses, such as photometric and landmark errors, against the input image. However, these losses enforce visual alignment but do not ensure that the predicted parameters preserve affective information. Recent methods add image-level emotion consistency loss, but it can be satisfied by exaggerating facial deformations. To address these issues, we propose FIELDS (Face reconstruction with accurate Inference of Expression using Learning with Direct Supervision), which learns affect-informative expression representations in the FLAME parameter space. Specifically, FIELDS augments 2D self-supervised reconstruction with scan-derived expression anchoring and a parameter-space emotion loss. During training, scan-fitted targets directly constrain expression-related FLAME parameters to discourage exaggerated deformations, while a jointly trained emotion head uses discrete emotion and continuous valence--arousal annotations to make the predicted parameters informative for affect analysis. Experiments show that FIELDS improves affective utility from the predicted parameters in both within- and cross-dataset settings. Notably, it also achieves lower reconstruction errors overall and across most facial regions than the comparison baselines under both rigid and similarity alignment.

item.title: JoVox: Joint Hierarchical Flow Matching for Lightweight Voxel Generation
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Xiangjun Tang, Jianqi Chen, Peter Wonka
arXiv:2611.10690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating high-fidelity voxels while keeping their lightweight nature remains an open problem in computer vision. Current generators are either high-fidelity but computationally heavy, or lightweight but of lower fidelity. Hierarchical methods keep the lightweight nature of voxels. However, their coarse levels, which decide where all finer cells can appear, are generated with the least information about the shape and are never revisited, so they are often plausible but wrong. Our key insight is to let finer cells take part in deciding coarse cells. To this end, we propose JoVox, a discrete flow matching framework that learns the joint distribution of all levels of the voxel hierarchy, instead of a separate distribution for each level, so that coarse cells can be predicted with finer cells already generated nearby. Within this framework, we further introduce a two-level prediction, which outputs the cells two levels finer at once instead of one level finer, halving the number of levels that the network processes and yielding voxels of higher fidelity. We also introduce an unmasking strategy that revisits early decisions once finer cells are generated and corrects inconsistencies in masked diffusion models. Our framework outperforms the baselines on both unconditional and image-conditioned voxel generation. Compared with the current state-of-the-art TRELLIS.2, we achieve 8x higher training throughput, 1/15 of the FLOPs in a forward pass, train on 4 vs. 32 GPUs, and obtain higher quality with an 11% lower Chamfer distance.

item.title: ArtCrafter: Feed-Forward Generation of Articulated 3D Object with Analytic Joint Derivation
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Minh Canh Tu, Quang-Binh Nguyen, Khoi Nguyen
arXiv:2611.07658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Articulated 3D assets are essential for robotic simulation and training, yet their generation from casual images poses a key challenge: recovering part geometry and kinematics that remain mutually consistent. We present ArtCrafter, a novel feed-forward generative model for controllable generation of articulated 3D objects from a pair of images, one depicting the object in the rest state and the other in the open state. At the core of ArtCrafter is a DiT-based generative model that jointly produces part-level meshes for both articulation states in a single forward pass. Inspired by Slot Attention, its denoising process operates on a $1+2N$ slot layout comprising one shared base slot and $N$ paired rest/open slots, encouraging each pair to bind to the same kinematic part. To ensure geometrically consistent and disjoint part generation, we introduce Triplet Attention to enforce cross-state geometric consistency between paired rest/open slots anchored through the shared base slot, and a repulsion loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rep}}$ on decoded part point clouds to prevent inter-part penetration throughout denoising. Given the resulting paired meshes, URDF joint parameters---type, axis, origin, and range---are derived analytically from the rigid transformation between each rest/open pair, providing an interpretable alternative to learned joint-parameter regression. Extensive experiments on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets demonstrate that ArtCrafter outperforms existing method under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision, while remaining competitive with methods operating under different input settings and paradigms.

item.title: A four-view smartphone video dataset of a robot-held flexible strip, with camera poses and a 3D LaGSplat baseline
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Louen Pottier
arXiv:2611.09959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This note describes a multi-view video dataset of a deformable object driven by a measured input, with the measured pose of every camera, and a first 3D result obtained on it with LaGSplat. LaGSplat learns from video a low-dimensional latent state that is both the generalized coordinate of a learned dissipative Lagrangian and the conditioning variable of a Gaussian Splatting decoder; fitting the decoder in 3D calls for synchronized multi-view footage, which the original paper only had from synthetic renderings. Here a robot arm moves a flexible strip by oscillating along a one-dimensional path, and four iPhones, three fixed and one handheld, film it for ten minutes. The videos are synchronized, the cameras are posed from the scene, and the position of the gripper is given per frame as the input of the system. LaGSplat fitted on this data with the gripper acceleration as a forcing term renders held-out views at 26 to 33 dB PSNR and runs as a real-time interactive demo in a web browser. Dataset, checkpoints and training code are public.

item.title: Learning a Maximum Entropy Model for Visual Textures using Diffusion
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Xinyuan Zhao, Eero P. Simoncelli
arXiv:2606.17342v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Visual textures -- spatially homogeneous image regions containing repeated elements (e.g. a field of grass, the bark of a tree) -- are ubiquitous in visual scenes and provide important cues for recognizing and analyzing materials, surface geometry and objects. A number of existing texture models extract essential statistics from a single texture image, and can then generate high-quality samples that are visually similar to the original by matching these statistics. However, their statistics are either hand-designed or based on a network pretrained for another purpose (e.g., object recognition). Here, we develop the first principled method for unsupervised learning of a set of statistics that are used to constrain a maximum entropy probability model for texture. We leverage methods developed for generative diffusion models to derive training and sampling procedures, and compare these to the traditional method of sampling via matching the statistics. Despite the compactness of our trained model (512 statistics), it generates texture images whose quality is as good as or better than the current state-of-the-art model (~177k statistics), both visually and by quantitative perceptual scoring using DreamSim. Finally, we show that images generated from parameters lying along a line between the parameter vectors corresponding to two different reference textures are homogeneous textures with features that smoothly transition between those of the two references.

item.title: Same Contacts, Different Rooms:Meeting Format Shapes LLM Group Influence Beyond Pairwise Contact Counts
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Physics and Society
Zhexi Gu, Shusheng Cao, Runping Zhu
arXiv:2611.10641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Simulations of LLM agent collectives usually summarise interaction as a pairwise contact network. We test that summary with a contact-matched intervention: the members, their initial stances and every pairwise contact count stay fixed while the meetings are reorganised, and each member gives a one-step support readout after reading the arguments of everyone present. Across six open-weight LLMs and 14 debate topics, merging triads into five-person meetings (resize) moves group support more than reshuffling who meets in triads (regroup), although both move the same 60 dyadic exposures. The root-mean-square change is 4.36 versus 2.59 percentage points (pp), larger for resize in all six models and in 81 of 84 model-topic cells. Resizing also has a consistent direction: it amplifies the initial majority of the merged members by 1.72 pp, in every model, whereas regrouping has no direction (<= 0.03 pp). A contact network cannot represent regrouping at all, yet pairwise rules applied meeting by meeting explain up to 76% of its effect, and with identical weights they raise resize R^2 by 0.51-0.58 for two models. We show that the gap between the two placements is an exact Jensen gap of the sigmoid readout, bounded by how much a member's predicted logits vary across meetings; this dispersion tracks the gap with log-log r=0.97 and tells a modeller when contact counts are a safe summary. Meeting format is a first-class variable for LLM social simulation.

item.title: Off-Policy RL with Online Inference Tuning: My Solution to the CoRL 2026 RoboEval Challenge
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Ilia Larchenko
arXiv:2611.11464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The CoRL 2026 RoboEval challenge has eight bimanual tasks, and it ranks a policy not only on whether it succeeds but on how: every stage of the task, done safely, efficiently and with both arms in coordination, scored against human demonstrations. My solution has two parts. The generic part, carried over from my LeHome challenge solution, is off-policy RL on a $\pi_{0.5}$-based policy that is also its own value function. It is trained with AWR and RECAP on advantages of the exact official score, in a loop where every rollout is at the same time a Thompson-sampling trial of about 20 inference parameters. Out of the box, it took the policy to 0.85 RDS on held-out seeds in two days (and it was still very far from convergence). The competition-specific part adds data that local exploration cannot find: generated demonstrations that reach the full reward, and recovery episodes that start from the policy's own failures. The submitted policy reaches 0.990 RDS on held-out seeds and 0.987 on the official seeds.

item.title: MoSTE: Mixture of Spatio-Temporal Experts for Deepfake Detection in Videos
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Charbel Yahchouchi, Nabyl Quignon, Noemi Roggero, Laurent Saroul, Antitza Dantcheva
arXiv:2611.12443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalizable deepfake video detection remains challenging because forgery artifacts vary substantially across manipulation types and often combine diverse spatial and temporal inconsistencies. Existing parameter-efficient adaptation methods typically rely on a single shared representation, rendering them prone to manipulation-specific bias and limiting transfer to unseen forgeries. To address this challenge, we propose Mixture Of Spatio-Temporal Experts (MoSTE), an adaptation framework that enables conditional specialization of forensic representations. Instead of forcing one adapter to model all forgery patterns, MoSTE decomposes adaptation into parallel spatial and temporal expert pools and dynamically routes tokens to the most relevant experts through an unsupervised token-level routing mechanism. This allows experts to naturally specialize in complementary forgery cues without requiring explicit manipulation labels or multi-stage training, while effectively transferring representations from CLIP to the video domain. Extensive experiments across cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that MoSTE sets a new state of the art in average generalization while preserving strong performance across diverse manipulation families. Additional analysis of expert routing and attention behavior reveals the emergence of expert diversity, suggesting that MoSTE learns complementary spatio-temporal forensic features. Code is available at https://github.com/charbelyah/MoSTE

item.title: RigidGS: Geometry-Aware Object Decoupling for Rigid-Body Interaction in 3D Gaussian Splatting
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Paul Sansah Gyreyiri, Diksha Shukla
arXiv:2611.10199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive VR/MR applications demand photorealistic 3D representations that support real-time rendering and object-level manipulation. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves high rendering quality, it represents scenes as unstructured, monolithic primitives. Existing object-aware 3DGS methods jointly optimize geometry and semantic states but suffer from two key failure modes: noisy foundation-model masks on complex geometry, and label-geometry coupling, in which co-optimized identity gradients mislabel boundary Gaussians. We introduce RigidGS, an end-to-end pipeline that decouples geometric learning from object identity. We propose a depth- and temporally-aware mask refinement module that addresses two complementary SAM2 failures: over-inclusion on thin structures and under-inclusion on multimodal-depth objects. We then determine object identities entirely upstream via COLMAP projection voting and freeze them during training, directing mask supervision solely toward geometric optimization. Refined masks alone substantially improve competing methods, yet a residual gap in label-geometry coupling persists that our fixed-identity design eliminates. RigidGS outperforms prior object-aware 3DGS methods on LLFF/NVOS, Mip-NeRF~360, and iNeRF360, improving segmentation and boundary IoU by 7.7 and 14.5 points on LLFF/NVOS. Finally, RigidGS enables real-time rigid-body manipulation on Meta Quest~2 without mesh extraction. Our code and project page are available at https://gyreyirisansah.github.io/rigidgs.

item.title: Confusion-Adaptive Margin Learning for Handwritten Letter Recognition: A Controlled Study on EMNIST Letters
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Azam Nouri
arXiv:2611.09953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Handwritten character recognition systems can achieve high accuracy while retaining concentrated errors among visually similar classes. Motivated by residual letter confusions in earlier geometry-based recognition work, we investigate whether these errors can be addressed through the training objective. We introduce Confusion-Adaptive Margin Learning (CAML), which constructs a sparse weighted confusion graph from a discovery partition held out from pilot training and applies pair-specific cosine-separation constraints during final training. CAML adds no classifier, routing rule, or inference-time parameters. We evaluate CAML on EMNIST Letters against a strictly matched cross-entropy CNN baseline, using the same architecture, final training data, deterministic augmentation, optimizer, and checkpoint selection. Eight confusion pairs are targeted: I/L, G/Q, U/V, R/V, D/O, C/E, I/J, and H/N. On the official clean test set, accuracy changes from 95.6346% to 95.6731%, and macro-F1 from 0.956326 to 0.956724. Mean accuracy across ten predefined corrupted conditions increases from approximately 95.3812% to 95.4303%; symmetric errors within targeted pairs decrease from 614 to 605 (1.47%). The global differences are small and not statistically reliable. CAML fixes 124 baseline errors but introduces 116 new errors on clean data (exact McNemar p=0.6515), and no corruption-specific difference remains significant after Holm correction. Thus, CAML does not establish global superiority, but shows that a leakage-controlled, pair-specific margin objective can alter targeted error structure with limited overall benefit for an already strong classifier.

item.title: Grasping the Future: Joint 3D Hand-Object Forecasting From Internet Videos
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Rustin Soraki, Matthew Wallingford, Ryan Aby, Brandon Chee, Jason Ren, Ali Farhadi, Homanga Bharadhwaj, Roozbeh Mottaghi
arXiv:2611.12879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To interact with an object, we need to anticipate both how it will move and how our hands should move with it. Human videos capture these relationships across everyday activities, offering a natural source for learning to predict future interactions. Learning from them requires recovering motion from completed interactions and using it to anticipate what could happen next. We present $\textit{Grasping-the-Future}$, a unified generative model of joint 3D hand-object motion, including wrist motion, finger articulation, and object position and orientation. Through masked spatiotemporal completion and flow matching, we train a single model for several prediction tasks: forecasting future interactions, predicting hand motion given object motion or vice versa, generating both trajectories toward a desired final object pose, and completing partially observed interactions. We explicitly model hand-object relations and incorporate contact constraints to help preserve grasp relationships during motion. To obtain 3D supervision from internet videos, we develop a scalable pipeline that combines pretrained perception models with joint geometric optimization to reconstruct completed interactions. We combine these recovered trajectories with annotated interaction datasets as training data for all tasks. We demonstrate strong performance across all tasks, outperforming released forecasters on datasets with 3D annotations. Moreover, we show geometric and physical plausibility of the predicted trajectories by retargeting them to a robotic embodiment. Videos are available at https://grasping-the-future.github.io.

item.title: PointForward: Feedforward Driving Reconstruction through Point-Aligned Representations
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Cheng Chi, Xianqi Wang, Hongcheng Luo, Mingfei Tu, Gangwei Xu, Zehan Zhang, Bing Wang, Guang Chen, Hangjun Ye, Sida Peng, Xin Yang, Haiyang Sun
arXiv:2605.11594v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-fidelity reconstruction of driving scenes is crucial for autonomous driving. While recent feedforward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods enable fast reconstruction, their per-pixel Gaussian prediction paradigm often suffers from multi-view inconsistency and layering artifacts. Moreover, existing methods often model dynamic instances via dense flow prediction, which lacks explicit cross-view correspondence and instance-level consistency. In this paper, we propose PointForward, a feedforward driving reconstruction framework through point-aligned representations. Unlike pixel-aligned methods, we initialize sparse 3D queries in world space and aggregate multi-view image information via spatial-temporal fusion onto these queries, enforcing explicit cross-view consistency in a single feedforward pass. To handle scene dynamics, we introduce scene graphs that explicitly organize moving instances during reconstruction. By leveraging 3D bounding boxes, our method enables instance-level motion propagation and temporally consistent dynamic representations. Extensive experiments show that PointForward achieves state-of-the-art performance on large-scale driving benchmarks.

item.title: Answer or Defer? Testing VLMs' Stated Confidence on Brain MRI
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Amir Sabbaghziarani, Parsa Ghazvinian, Sepehr Salem, Sergey Plis
arXiv:2611.11833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) could support medical-image interpretation, but their use requires deciding which interpretations to accept and which images to refer to a clinician. We test whether thresholding stated confidence can retain useful coverage while limiting errors among accepted answers, and how this depends on the population. Eight open-weight VLMs, including two reasoning models, assess 3,888 brain MRI slices from post-treatment glioma patients (BraTS 2024) and healthy volunteers (IXI) for tumor or gross abnormality. BraTS labels are mask-derived; IXI slices are treated as negatives. On BraTS, no threshold selects a nonempty set with at most 5% empirical error for any model, even when chosen retrospectively. This also holds for four models evaluated on a large-lesion, distant-negative subset. At a 10% error budget, Gemma-4-12B retains 24.4% of slices and every other model at most 2.5%. To investigate this limited selection ability, we separate confidence differences between predicted answers from differences within each answer. For four models with available outcome-level summaries, pooled mean confidence differs more between answers than between correct and incorrect responses within each answer. A covariance decomposition explains how this pattern can produce opposite confidence-correctness associations across populations. At a 20% error budget, accepting every "tumor" answer covers more slices than any confidence threshold for two models. These findings caution against using unvalidated stated confidence as a standalone deferral signal and support population-specific validation before deployment. Code is available at https://github.com/amir-sbg/VLM-Answer-or-Defer.

item.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Hao Yu, Zhenwei Wang, Yongzhen Hu, Yuning Gong, Junta Wu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Tengfei Wang, Chunchao Guo, Sida Peng
arXiv:2611.08264v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision. To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SplatAnything

item.title: TimeTraveler: Temporal Strategy Planning with Time Dictionary for Streaming Video Understanding
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Minkuk Kim, Junho Kim, Seong Tae Kim
arXiv:2611.10337v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Streaming video understanding (SVU) requires models to answer user queries over continuously evolving video streams. Unlike offline video QA, SVU must handle queries whose evidence may lie in the past, appear in the current scene, or emerge only after future observations. Existing streaming video systems often rely on compact visual memories or fixed evidence-access schemes, which can lose fine-grained details and fail to adapt the answering process to the temporal intent of each query. In this paper, we propose TimeTraveler, a streaming VQA framework that performs temporal strategy planning with a Time Dictionary. Inspired by the need to search across different temporal regions of a stream, TimeTraveler stores each observed moment as a timestamp-indexed structured caption and uses this dictionary as an explicit source of queryable evidence. Given a query, TimeTraveler determines whether to recall past evidence, read the present context, or wait for future observations, and then applies a strategy-specific evidence acquisition process. Comparative experiments on streaming video QA benchmarks show that TimeTraveler improves streaming question answering by preserving fine-grained temporal evidence and selecting the appropriate temporal strategy for each query. The project page is available at https://geppa.github.io/TimeTraveler.

item.title: FOCUS: Benchmarking Retinal Model Generalization from Foundation Vision Encoders to Multimodal LLMs
item.description:
Relevance: 21% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
David Restrepo, Chenwei Wu, Luis Filipe Nakayama, Miguel L. Martins, Stergios Christodoulidis, Maria Vakalopoulou, Enzo Ferrante
arXiv:2609.33158v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Progress in AI-based retinal image analysis has accelerated with the adoption of foundation models, yet evaluating their real-world reliability remains challenging. Performance reported on a single dataset does not capture how models behave under dataset shift, across clinical definitions, or for different patient subgroups. This limitation is particularly critical in medical imaging, where robustness, calibration, and fairness are essential for safe deployment. We introduce FOCUS (Foundation Ophthalmic Cross-Dataset Understanding under Shift), a cross-dataset benchmark evaluating retinal fundus models across vision-only encoder models (VM), vision-language dual-encoder models (VLM), and multimodal large language models (MLLM). FOCUS harmonizes binary diabetic retinopathy, referable diabetic retinopathy, and glaucomatous optic neuropathy tasks across ten public datasets spanning diverse geographies, acquisition conditions, and label protocols. The benchmark evaluates models through a unified analysis layer that measures ranking performance, calibration, subgroup disparities, and image-quality robustness. We present a large-scale evaluation covering 532 base configurations and 228 MLLM configurations adapted via LoRA fine-tuning. Results show no model family consistently dominates across tasks and datasets: general VM encoders achieve the strongest average ranking performance, medical MLLMs are competitive but variable, and dual-encoder VLMs benefit substantially from lightweight adaptation. Fine-tuning improves in-domain performance but exhibits heterogeneous transfer to external datasets, particularly in calibration. FOCUS provides a practical framework and public benchmark to assess generalization, reliability, and robustness beyond single-dataset leaderboards.

item.title: VLM as an Editing Pilot: VLM-Steered Velocity Control for Flow-Based Image Editing
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Kuan-Shen Chiu, Jia-Wei Liao, Yu-Chieh Chao, Li-Xuan Peng, Wei-Yun Ma, Cheng-Fu Chou
arXiv:2611.10066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-guided image editing requires realizing the requested semantic change while preserving content unrelated to the instruction. FlowEdit provides an efficient inversion-free solution, but its source-anchored coupling can become overly restrictive, causing zero-edit, where the output remains close to the source and the requested change fails to emerge. We find that source coupling directly governs the preservation--editing trade-off, while a fixed coupling schedule cannot adapt to timestep-specific editing needs. Motivated by this observation, we propose V2C-Edit, a training-free VLM-steered velocity control framework. V2C-Edit constructs complementary coupling-controlled velocities and dynamically selects among them using Instruction-Level Similarity (ILS), which evaluates whether the predicted transformation follows the editing instruction. Adaptive spatial masking further preserves regions unrelated to the edit. Experiments on MagicBrush and PIE-Bench with FLUX and Stable Diffusion 3 show that V2C-Edit consistently improves instruction alignment over FlowEdit while maintaining competitive structural preservation, and that ILS better reflects editing effectiveness than target-caption CLIP similarity. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kuanshen77/V2C-Edit.

item.title: SceneShifter: Training-free Multi-Scene Temporal Control for Audio-driven Human Animation
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Jianzhi Long, Rong-Cheng Tu, Hao Guan, Siyuan Liang, Shunyu Liu, Xiao Luo, Dacheng Tao
arXiv:2611.09960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although audio-driven human animation has achieved impressive realism, it still lacks effective Multi-Scene Temporal Control: orchestrating background transitions at precise timestamps while preserving a coherent foreground subject. We show that this challenge stems from the diffusion transformer's self-attention mechanism, and addressing it requires two capabilities: (1) Semantic-Aware Temporal Decoupling, which isolates background attention across scenes while retaining cross-scene foreground attention for subject consistency; and (2) Foreground Motion Localization, which accurately tracks the foreground subject across latent frames, especially under large motion. To address these challenges, we introduce SceneShifter, a training-free framework for precise multi-scene control in audio-driven human animation. SceneShifter guides spatio-temporal self-attention by suppressing cross-scene attention among background tokens while preserving cross-scene attention among foreground tokens. To support this guidance under large motion, SceneShifter extracts dynamic foreground masks from the self-attention layers and heads that best capture subject trajectories. We further introduce SceneShifterBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate scene-timing accuracy, foreground preservation, and visual quality under large motion, multiple subjects. Experiments show that SceneShifter achieves frame-level scene timing, strong subject preservation, and high visual quality, outperforming existing baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/JamesLong199/SceneShifter.

item.title: ROLECUE: Diagnosing Cross-Lingual Role-Binding Failures in Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Niaz Mohaiman Abtahi, Evan Maksud
arXiv:2611.10575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can recognize events in images and parse sentences, but it remains unclear when they bind visual Agent-Patient structure to linguistic semantic roles across languages whose role cues depend on morphology, word order or construction. We introduce ROLECUE, a controlled diagnostic that pairs 192 validated two-person action images with German, Turkish, Japanese, English, Korean and Bangla sentences in canonical and patient-first orders. The evaluation separates image-only role recognition, text-only role parsing, direct image-sentence matching, response-compliance behavior and an external modular composition of the model's own component predictions. Across eight recent open-weight VLMs, ROLECUE reveals a structured spectrum: some models fail visual or linguistic component tests, some largely solve the diagnostic, some collapse to constant semantic assent and several show component-joint gaps in which reliable image-only and text-only role predictions do not survive direct joint inference. The largest non-degenerate gaps reach 44.9 percentage points, with final bootstrap intervals confirming that the effect is not a point-estimate artifact. These results reveal multilingual component-joint performance gaps and acceptance biases hidden by aggregate VLM benchmarks and show why component diagnostics are necessary before interpreting joint multimodal errors.

item.title: UDT: Reconciling U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers with Data-Adaptive Token Reduction
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Junno Yun, Ya\c{s}ar Utku Al\c{c}alar, Mehmet Ak\c{c}akaya
arXiv:2608.01298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as a core architecture in generative modeling due to their scalability and adaptability to multimodal tasks. DiTs comprise isotropic transformer blocks, and learn representations progressively across depth, where the denoising objective drives later layers to focus on fine-detail reconstruction. This results in degraded representation quality and an imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior. Prior approaches such as representation alignment (REPA) mitigate this by encouraging stronger early representations via training regularization. Alternatively, U-Net-style DiT architectures introduce explicit multi-scale encoder-decoder structures for improved convergence. But they build on standard U-Net wisdom via learnable operators for spatial downsampling, which are not well-suited to transformer architectures, introducing inefficiencies and compatibility issues with components such as cross-attention and representation regularization. In this work, we propose UDT, a U-Net diffusion transformer that combines the representation power of DiTs with the encoding-decoding benefits of U-Nets, through data-adaptive token merging for downsampling and upsampling, while preserving the DiT token dimension. Our baseline UDT architecture outperforms existing U-Net DiTs and achieves performance comparable to REPA across all model sizes. Furthermore, using architectural optimization and REPA, UDT outperforms SiT's 7.9 FID at 1400 epochs (w/o CFG) within 40 epochs (~ 40x faster convergence) for XL model size on 256x256 ImageNet. Finally, it achieves strong image generation performance with CFG, reaching FID of 1.38 (320 epochs) with SD-VAE and 1.35 (500 epochs) with VA-VAE, providing a new backbone for DiTs with strong empirical benefits. Code is available at https://github.com/JN-Yun/UDT

item.title: ChartHal: A Fine-grained Framework Evaluating Hallucination of Large Vision Language Models in Chart Understanding
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Xingqi Wang, Yiming Cui, Xin Yao, Shijin Wang, Guoping Hu, Xiaoyu Qin
arXiv:2509.17481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have recently demonstrated remarkable progress, yet hallucination remains a critical barrier, particularly in chart understanding, which requires sophisticated perceptual and cognitive abilities as well as rigorous factual accuracy. While prior work has investigated hallucinations and chart comprehension independently, their intersection remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we present ChartHal, a benchmark that features a fine-grained taxonomy of hallucination scenarios in chart understanding, along with a human-validated dataset of 1,062 samples. Our evaluation shows that state-of-the-art LVLMs suffer from severe hallucinations on ChartHal, including proprietary models such as GPT-5 and o4-mini, which achieve only 34.46% and 22.79% accuracy, respectively. Further analysis reveals that questions involving information absent from or contradictory to charts are especially likely to trigger hallucinations, underscoring the urgent need for more robust mitigation strategies. Code and data are available at https://github.com/ymcui/ChartHal

item.title: RedPhys: An Extensible Red-Teaming Platform for Physical-World Models and Agents
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Yifei Zhao, Qian Lou, Mengxin Zheng
arXiv:2606.23892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Physical-world models (PhyModels) perform grounded perception, reasoning, or decision tasks; physical-world agents (PhyAgents) combine these models with planning or tool use. We introduce RedPhys, an extensible red-teaming platform, instantiated here with vision-language models and agents. Shared interfaces make tasks, test methods, defenses, and victim systems configurable and extensible, producing robustness reports and datasets for future alignment. The platform emphasizes adversarial testing that seeks physically grounded functional failures, while also supporting non-adversarial input perturbations without an attack objective. The benchmark integrates 12 red-teaming methods, 3 model-agnostic defenses, and 13 PhyModels across seven physical domains under a practical black-box threat model. An agentic target-generation pipeline derives a scene-specific, physically grounded target, so targeted methods pursue the same intended error. Our evaluation shows that when attackers control the text prompt or add auxiliary visual instructions, injection exposes substantial instruction-following vulnerabilities; among bounded visual-transfer attacks, multimodal co-optimization transfers best; single-pass generative attacks approach iterative methods without per-image optimization; and neither model scale nor physical-reasoning post-training confers robustness. Code is available at https://github.com/loopleap-lab/RedPhys.

item.title: ContraSafe-VL: A Contrastive Safety Preference Dataset for Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Di Wu, Yanyan Zhao, Xin Lu, Hao Yang, Taotao Zhang, Yunzhen Zhao
arXiv:2610.23908v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed as general-purpose multimodal assistants, making multimodal safety alignment an important challenge. Safety depends on the interplay between textual and visual content, with visual context often playing a critical role. However, VLMs may fail to use visual information appropriately, either overlooking safety-relevant visual content or over-interpreting sensitive visual content, leading to unsafe responses or over-refusal. Existing multimodal safety alignment datasets largely follow the response-preference paradigm, which teaches models how to respond but provides limited supervision on how visual context should inform the safety judgment, making it difficult to balance safety and over-refusal. To address this limitation, we introduce \textbf{ContraSafe-VL}, a \textbf{Contra}stive \textbf{Safe}ty preference dataset for \textbf{V}ision-\textbf{L}anguage Models. For each fixed textual query, ContraSafe-VL constructs paired visual contexts that result in multimodal queries with different safety labels, providing direct supervision for how visual context should inform multimodal safety judgments. It further provides response preference pairs based on harmlessness and helpfulness to encourage models to generate responses that are both safe and helpful. Experiments across three VLM architectures and multiple benchmarks demonstrate that training with ContraSafe-VL improves cross-modal safety recognition and achieves a better safety--over-refusal trade-off while preserving general multimodal capabilities. The dataset is available at https://github.com/pikepokenew/ContraSafe-VL

item.title: FFM-CP: Cross-Backbone Fusion of Vision-Language Foundation Models for Few-Shot Computational Pathology
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Anh-Tien Nguyen, Trung Dang, Nghiem Tuong Diep, Bui Ngoc Han Nguyen, Tan-Ha Mai, Miriam Cindy Maurer, Phuong Hoa Nguyen, Thi Thuy Uyen Nguyen, Youngjun Park, Daniel Sonntag, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Anne-Christin Hauschild
arXiv:2609.27710v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pathology vision-language foundation models vary in performance across diseases and tasks, with no single model consistently performing best. The high cost of expert pathology annotation can also limit the labeled data available for task-specific adaptation. Combining complementary pretrained representations is a potential approach to these limitations, yet learning an effective fusion from few labeled examples remains challenging. We introduce Few-shot Fusion Foundation Models of Computational Pathology (FFM-CP), which is a framework that combines multiple pathology vision-language models in the few-shot learning setting. The framework first aligns heterogeneous representations using a closed-form Orthogonal Procrustes transformation estimated from corresponding support images. This alignment preserves within-model feature geometry without training an additional alignment network. Within the aligned space, a unified graph enables information exchange across backbones by jointly refining support-image features and visual and textual class prototypes. These refined representations support complementary text-prototype and case-retrieval branches that capture semantic class knowledge and within-class visual variation, respectively. Each branch learns to combine predictions from all ordered backbone pairs, allowing queries encoded by one model to draw on evidence represented by another. We evaluate three backbone combinations on six histopathology datasets at 4, 8, and 16 shots per class. FFM-CP achieves higher mean macro-F1 than the strongest individually adapted member of each fused set in 50 of 54 comparisons. These findings suggest that combining complementary pretrained representations can improve histopathological classification when annotations are limited.

item.title: Reason First, Retrieve What Matters: Hypothesis-Guided Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Yisong Hu, Junbo Wang, Yuke Li, Jiangbin Zheng
arXiv:2611.10609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long video understanding requires models to identify and reason over sparse, temporally distributed evidence within limited frame budgets. Existing keyframe selection methods typically retrieve query-relevant frames from a densely sampled candidate set before inference. However, global image-text matching incurs unnecessary computation when a small set of uniformly sampled frames already provides sufficient evidence. Query relevance alone may also overlook evidence that distinguishes competing answers, while one-shot selection offers no opportunity to correct earlier selection errors. We propose HypoKFS, a training-free, plug-and-play framework that couples keyframe selection with iterative inference by multimodal large language models (MLLMs). HypoKFS first reasons over sparsely sampled frames to construct an initial hypothesis space. The resulting answer distribution determines whether additional frame selection is needed. When needed, the retained hypotheses guide the selection of discriminative frames, followed by renewed inference and hypothesis refinement. This iterative process directs additional visual computation toward unresolved hypotheses while avoiding unnecessary global frame matching. Experiments on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple MLLM backbones. HypoKFS improves accuracy by up to 6.7 percentage points and achieves 72.9% accuracy on Video-MME at only 1.3% of the reference frame-hypothesis matching cost.

item.title: EarthJev: Efficient Visual Evidence Acquisition and Decision for UHR Remote Sensing Understanding
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Pengyu Dai, Yao Zhang, Jian Song, Junjue Wang, Yafei Ou, Yuzeng Chen, Junshi Xia, Hongruixuan Chen, Naoto Yokoya
arXiv:2611.10005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing visual question answering (VQA) requires locating fine-grained evidence in large scenes under limited visual input budgets. Active observation addresses this challenge through selective exploration, but repeated generative judgments can make region search costly. Its decisions also concern distinct prediction targets: spatial pointer validity, evidence presence, and reasoning correctness. We propose EarthJev, a framework that separates region scoring from answer generation and uses target-specific decision signals while keeping the answering model frozen. A spatial pointer verifier uses visual and geometric cues to guide exploration or bypass search. An evidence-aware decision mechanism scores compact candidate views in batches using a lightweight head on frozen representations, without generating textual region judgments. Format-specific confidence calibration then guides selection between candidate answers generated from memory and overview presentations of the acquired evidence. Across five benchmarks, EarthJev achieves a mean accuracy of 53.06% with Qwen3.5-9B, outperforming ZoomSearch with the same answering model by 2.33 to 14.73 percentage points per benchmark while reducing mean latency from 11.30 - 1.67 seconds per question. With four additional frozen answering models, model-specific fitting of the decision modules and calibration mappings yields mean accuracy gains of 3.41 - 6.53 percentage points over the corresponding single-pass baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/Da1daidaidai/EarthJev

item.title: Temporally Ordered Region-Token Mamba with Logit-Space Diffusion for Remote Sensing Change Detection
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Maneet Chatterjee, Aparup Ghosh, Anuvab Sen, Udayon Sen, Arnav Aditya, Yixin Zhang
arXiv:2609.27149v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Change Detection (CD) in remote sensing requires jointly modeling bitemporal context and fine-grained spatial details to accurately localize changed regions. While dense attention effectively captures bitemporal relationships, its computational cost limits scalability to high-resolution imagery. In contrast, conventional feature fusion and coarse decoding often struggle to distinguish true changes from appearance variations and preserve object boundaries. To overcome these limitations, we propose Bitemporal Mamba-Diffusion for Change Detection (BMD-CD), a framework that integrates temporally structured state-space modeling with logit-space diffusion refinement. BMD-CD first converts deep bitemporal features into region tokens and organizes them into explicit temporal partitions for bidirectional state-space propagation. It then employs a Learnable Trigonometric Fusion (LTF) module to integrate temporal information and a Conditional Diffusion Decoder that refines coarse predictions in logit space with a short DDIM schedule to generate fine-grained, high-resolution change maps. Extensive experiments on LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, DSIFN-CD, CDD, and S2Looking demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. BMD-CD achieves IoU scores of 0.923, 0.957, 0.882, and 0.979 on WHU-CD, DSIFN-CD, LEVIR-CD, and CDD, respectively, and further exhibits strong zero-shot robustness on ValaisCD and B-FLAIR-test.

item.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Zhimin Liao, Ping Wei, Kai Mao, Shuaijia Chen
arXiv:2611.11912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy represent two distinct modalities capturing fine-grained metric geometry and dense volumetric semantics, respectively, holding natural potential for mutual complementarity. However, existing world models typically forecast these modalities independently or cascade them heuristically, missing the opportunity for reciprocal cross-modal regularization. To address this, we propose \textbf{LO-World}, a unified 4D world model that forecasts both modalities within a shared BEV latent space. This single-stream formulation enables dense semantics and metric geometry to mutually reinforce each other, while eliminating multi-pipeline redundancy. Specifically, LO-World couples an efficient hybrid range-voxel autoencoder with a flow-matching generator that caches historical context to reduce iterative sampling latency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LO-World outperforms prior state-of-the-art baselines, improving occupancy forecasting IoU by 10.9% and reducing LiDAR Chamfer Distance by 30.1%. Meanwhile, it sustains a real-time throughput exceeding $25$~FPS on a single RTX 4090. Our code is available at https://github.com/lzzzzzm/LO-World.

item.title: Learning Pathology-Sensitive Representations for Unsupervised Retinal OCT Anomaly Detection
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Tania Haghighi, Sina Gholami, Behafarin Emam, Jennifer I Lim, Theodore Leng, Atalie C Thompson, Hamed Tabkhi, Minhaj Nur Alam
arXiv:2610.33143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep learning approaches for retinal optical coherence tomography (OCT) predominantly rely on predefined disease categories, limiting their ability to detect rare or previously unseen abnormalities. While visual foundation models provide transferable representations, their effectiveness in identifying pathological deviations from normal retinal anatomy remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we introduce an unsupervised framework for retinal OCT anomaly detection and localization that adapts pretrained visual representations to normal retinal anatomy through anatomy-aware reconstruction and contrastive triplet learning guided by synthetic structural perturbations, without requiring disease-specific annotations. We systematically investigate the influence of pretraining strategies, anatomy-aware representation adaptation, and anomaly scoring mechanisms on the detection and localization of unseen retinal abnormalities. Our findings demonstrate that adapting pretrained representations to normal retinal structure improves anomaly sensitivity, while pixel-space reconstruction errors and feature-space deviations provide complementary signals for identifying pathological changes. These findings underscore the importance of anatomy-aware representation learning and offer insights into developing generalizable retinal anomaly detection frameworks beyond predefined disease categories.

item.title: A forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models: an EFM3D case study for crime scene reconstruction
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Davidson Chisom Onwubiko, Shahana Bano, Carlos Francisco Moreno-Garc\'ia
arXiv:2611.12259v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Foundation models increasingly combine geometry, semantics, and spatial context for three-dimensional scene understanding, but their suitability for forensic crime scene reconstruction remains unclear. This study presents a structured forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models and demonstrates it using the Egocentric Foundation Model for 3D (EFM3D). Four simulated indoor crime scenes were recorded with Meta Project Aria Gen~1 at Robert Gordon University's East Lodge House forensic training facility. The framework evaluates room-scale reconstruction, semantic scene understanding, computational performance, and forensic suitability. Across the four scenes, EFM3D generated meshes averaging $12{,}668\pm2{,}430$ vertices and $24{,}838\pm4{,}903$ faces, with 39,529 recorded semantic predictions spanning 21--24 categories at a mean confidence of 0.40. Because reference meshes and expert-labelled 3D ground truth were unavailable, these statistics are treated as descriptive outputs rather than measures of geometric or detection accuracy. Final inference runs processed $1{,}388\pm203$ snippets per scene at $0.69\pm0.01$ samples/s and required $50.77\pm6.12$ minutes per recording. A seven-criterion capability profile indicated stronger support for room geometry, furniture localisation, scene context, and spatial relationships than for fine-scale forensic evidence. The results position EFM3D as a complementary tool for contextual documentation and scene review rather than a replacement for high-fidelity forensic capture. The framework provides a reproducible basis for evaluating future egocentric foundation models in specialised forensic settings.

item.title: VETime: Vision Enhanced Zero-Shot Time Series Anomaly Detection
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Yingyuan Yang, Tian Lan, Yifei Gao, Yimeng Lu, Xuming An, Wenjun He, Meng Wang, Chenghao Liu, Chen Zhang
arXiv:2602.16681v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) requires identifying both immediate Point Anomalies and long-range Context Anomalies. However, existing foundation models face a fundamental trade-off: 1D temporal models provide fine-grained pointwise localization but lack a global contextual perspective, while 2D vision-based models capture global patterns but suffer from information bottlenecks due to a lack of temporal alignment and coarse-grained pointwise detection. To resolve this dilemma, we propose VETime, the first TSAD framework that unifies temporal and visual modalities through fine-grained visual-temporal alignment and dynamic fusion. VETime introduces a Reversible Image Conversion and a Patch-Level Temporal Alignment module to establish a shared visual-temporal timeline, preserving discriminative details while maintaining temporal sensitivity. Furthermore, we design an Anomaly Window Contrastive Learning mechanism and a Task-Adaptive Multi-Modal Fusion to adaptively integrate the complementary perceptual strengths of both modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VETime significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models in zero-shot scenarios, achieving superior localization precision with lower computational overhead than current vision-based approaches. Code available at: https://github.com/yyyangcoder/VETime .

item.title: Anatomy-Preserving Unpaired Medical Image Translation via Shared Latent Anchoring
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Zhilin Zou, Hieu Le, Saumya Gupta, Jingyi Xu, Prateek Prasanna, Chao Chen
arXiv:2611.10236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unpaired medical image-to-image translation requires synthesizing target-modality images from source-modality images without aligned supervision. Existing methods learn a direct source-to-target mapping that entangles structure preservation and appearance generation within a single model, often distorting clinically meaningful anatomy in the translated output. We argue that these two objectives should be decoupled entirely: anatomical structure should be captured independently of generation, and the generator should operate only on a frozen structural representation. To this end, we propose a two-stage framework for unpaired medical image translation. In the first stage, we learn a shared structure space by training a structure encoder-decoder on source images, target images, and structural masks jointly, using mask reconstruction to anchor the latent space to modality-agnostic anatomy. For source images without mask annotations, a target-domain memory bank provides soft structural supervision via prototype retrieval. In the second stage, a conditional flow model learns to render target-domain appearance under fixed structural conditions. This ensures the generator inherits target appearance statistics and can focus entirely on structural conditioning rather than learning appearance from scratch. We validate our framework on OCT-to-OCTA synthesis and brain MR-to-CT translation. Our method outperforms all unpaired baselines on both tasks and, despite requiring no paired supervision, also surpasses paired baselines, improving PSNR by up to 11.2% and SSIM by up to 26.4% on OCT-to-OCTA, and achieving consistent gains across whole-image, soft-tissue, and bone regions on MR-to-CT. The project repository is available on GitHub.

item.title: Quadratic Bezier Splatting with Structural Initialization for Efficient Painting Rendering
item.description:
Relevance: 20% | Source: arXiv Computer Vision
Jinfan Liu, Xuhan Zhan, Mengqin Zhao, Guangyi Deng, Wuze Zhang, Bingbing Ni
arXiv:2611.10713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stroke-based rendering is often optimized as a pixel-level reconstruction task. This over-reliance on global error reduction not only degrades strokes into fragmented curves due to a lack of structured planning, but also allows locally defective primitives to be concealed by overlapping layers. To address these issues, we introduce a model-guided framework for stroke-audited rendering. Our framework uses Quadratic Bezier Splatting to analytically model continuous curved strokes with efficient differentiable alpha compositing. Built on this renderer, a feedforward multi-scale stroke decoder provides a structural initialization with learned stroke-scale allocation, while test-time stroke optimization supplies the reconstruction capacity needed for high-fidelity refinement. We further propose a single-stroke audit mechanism that explicitly evaluates local stroke quality, preventing defective primitives from surviving optimization through layer-wise compensation. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves coherent layouts, improves PSNR by up to 5.46 dB, yields a 16% more compact representation, and accelerates combined renderer forward and backward computation by a factor of 220.3.

item.description:

Ryan Seamus McGeeOlivia KosterlitzArtem KaznatcheevBenjamin KerrCarl T.
